title: Security Deposits Rule on Trimming a Single Peak in the Recalculation Basis Bill
content:
In the recalculation of a held Security Deposits deposit, the recalculation basis bill trims a single peak in the bills of the recalculation window.

## Rule

When the highest bill in the window exceeds the window average by more than the high trim ratio of **1.6** — that is, when it is more than 1.6 times the window average — the basis bill is the average of the window's other bills, the highest one left out. When it is more than **1.3** times the window average but not more than 1.6 times it, the basis bill is the midpoint of that trimmed average and the window average. Otherwise the peak is not trimmed and the basis bill is the window average.

## Quantities

- **Bills:** a billing period's bill is the sum of that period's usage lines on the Electric Service by Rate Schedule account, read month by month back from today; the bills compared are those of the months inside the window.
- **Window average:** the usage lines billed in the window, added together, divided by the number of facility charge lines billed in the window.
- **Trimmed average:** the window's usage total less the highest bill, divided by one fewer than the number of facility charge lines in the window.

## Bands (hypothetical twelve-period window)

| Window total | Window average | Highest bill | Ratio | Trimmed average | Basis bill |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $1560.00 | $130.00 | $460.00 | 3.54 | $100.00 | $100.00 |
| $1320.00 | $110.00 | $176.00 | exactly 1.6 | $104.00 | $107.00, the midpoint |
| $1320.00 | $110.00 | $165.00 | 1.5 | $105.00 | $107.50, the midpoint |
| $1320.00 | $110.00 | $143.00 | exactly 1.3 | — | $110.00, not trimmed |
